questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It had to be a good university in an english speaking country, preferrably in the US or Canada. The main criterea was global university rankings of the university as well as the ranking of the economics department (as that is what I would be taking courses in). It was preferred if the university was located in or near a major city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UofT did provide me with basic information, for instance where I could pick up my ID card and what locations my courses took place in. However, I was given a digital tour of campus, which made little sense, as all the courses I took were in-person. I was not provided any help with housing (i applied for all colleges, and did not recieve any offers), so I had to find my own. We were provided with a facebook group, but overall the help from the University was quite minimal, I don't know if this was due to covid restrictions at the time I arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Again, the digital tour of campus. But that was it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Try to get into as many facebook groups for housing as possible and if you have a local contact be sure to contact them!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Toronto is expensive and difficult to find housing in. Be sure to try to find something as fast as possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My housing was great, but I found it on my own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not too much of a hassle, you will receive your utorid by mail which gives you access to all the digital information you need.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After sending in your application, UofT will send all the digital information you need periodically leading up to the semester start.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Regular E-Mail updates.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Medium, it was reasonably easy to get into courses in Economics (my major), but getting into courses outside of Economics was impossible for me (I tried to enroll in some math courses). The application process required A LOT of paperwork. You had to fill out a 3-page form individually for every single course you applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply early on, so you have plenty of time to find courses in case you are denied some in the first round.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the profs were really amazing, super interested in what they were teaching. I had one professor who taught a course requiring a lot of group work, who described how it was in every student's interest to contibute as little as possible to free-ride on other students. Needless to say this did not create a very cooperative enviroment (luckily the students taking the course were very nice and helpful). But he was likely a bad apple, as I enjoyed the four other courses I took where the professors treated their students very well.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I mainly took 3rd and 4rth year bachelors courses, as when I was applying to UofT i was still writing my bachelor's thesis, which was required to apply for MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A LOT more group work at UofT, of the five courses I took, three of them predominantly were group work. Secondly, in Denmark we usually have one big exam at the end of the course. At UofT, this is very different, as most courses have a midterm, a final, which each count about 30% and a bunch of small assignments spread out throughout the semester to cover the last 40%. The work load is a lot higher at UofT because of this, where a lot of the time is spent writing essays and making powerpoint slides rather than going through the material (in my opinion). However, you are not at risk of failing at the final exam in the same way at UofT because you are required to do a lot of course work during the semester, which is quite nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECO339 - Labour Economics
ECO349 - Money, Banking and Financial Markets
ECO365 - International monetary economics
ECO428 - Classical Economic Thought
ECO466 - Empirical Macro and Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ECO339 was really enjoyable, the professor gave absolutely amazing lectures with lots of interaction with the students.
ECO428 Was also great if you are interested in the history of economics, it is not exactly a standard economics course but I really enjoyed it

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: SIM card service is EXTREMELY expensive in Canada. Also, the books were more expensive than I was used to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was surprisingly expensive in Toronto, eating out in restaurants cost almost the same as buying food from your local grocery store (also due to eating in restaurants being quite cheap, about 75-85 DKK for a good sit-down meal). Rent is expensive, but not much worse than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: On the website most sports were seriously hindered by Covid restrictions.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Very little, maybe I didn't hear about them, or else they didnt happen because of Covid.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The gym was good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definately try to get out of the city into some of Ontarios nature. It is really amazing! Also take a trip to Quebec to see a completely different side of Canada.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Canadians are very welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yes, students were quite easy to talk to when you finally get the opportunity.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing super different really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are very polite and welcoming, I had the great opportunity to be invited to some cottages up north, which were absolutely spectacular experiences for me.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1 - The workload at UofT is very high, you should know this before going
2 - Definately try to socialize as much as possible in the very beginning of your semester so you get to meet people
3 - Get used to studying and working way before the final exams, as a lot of the grade is determined through smaller projects

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing more than the above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the locals and other exchange students. I met some really great people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting settled in. There are a lot of small things that need to be done when you arrive. Whether it is VISA stuff, finding housing, opening a bank account or figuring out the local shops/transportation. There are a lot of small things that end up taking a lot more time than you would think.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Be very careful when transferring money to canada, I made the mistake of using a bank transfer and was ripped off by the exchange fee, use a transfer service like transferwise or just use your visa card from Denmark whilst you are there.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
